name: earthengine
description: Google Earth Engine Code Editor functionalities brought to VS Code

earthengine.tasks.maxItems.description: Maximum number of tasks to display in the sidebar and panel tree views.

earthengine.tasks.scanLimit.description: Maximum number of operations to fetch from the API when loading or refreshing tasks.

earthengine.tasks.historyDays.description: Number of days of task history to load.

earthengine.map.basemap.light.markdownDescription: Overrides the built-in **light** basemap, used when VS Code is in a light colour theme. Accepts a Google Map Tiles [`createSession`](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/session_tokens) request body: `mapType`, `styles`, `layerTypes`, `overlay`, `scale`, `highDpi`, `imageFormat`. `styles` is only honoured when `mapType` is `roadmap` — build one with the [Styling Wizard](https://mapstyle.withgoogle.com/). Leave empty to use the built-in preset.

earthengine.map.basemap.dark.markdownDescription: Overrides the built-in **dark** basemap, used when VS Code is in a dark colour theme. Accepts a Google Map Tiles [`createSession`](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/session_tokens) request body. Design `styles` with the [Styling Wizard](https://mapstyle.withgoogle.com/). Leave empty to use the built-in preset.

earthengine.map.basemap.planLight.markdownDescription: Overrides the built-in **light plan** basemap, used by the plan toggle in a light colour theme. Accepts a Google Map Tiles [`createSession`](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/session_tokens) request body. Design `styles` with the [Styling Wizard](https://mapstyle.withgoogle.com/). Leave empty to use the built-in preset.

earthengine.map.basemap.planDark.markdownDescription: Overrides the built-in **dark plan** basemap, used by the plan toggle in a dark colour theme. Accepts a Google Map Tiles [`createSession`](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/session_tokens) request body. Design `styles` with the [Styling Wizard](https://mapstyle.withgoogle.com/). Leave empty to use the built-in preset.

earthengine.map.basemap.satellite.markdownDescription: Overrides the built-in **satellite** basemap, used by the satellite toggle. Accepts a Google Map Tiles [`createSession`](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/session_tokens) request body. `styles` is ignored unless `mapType` is `roadmap`. Leave empty to use the built-in preset.

earthengine.assets.staging.prefix.markdownDescription: Object prefix used inside the staging bucket when uploading a local file for ingestion. The bucket itself is chosen in the **New asset** dialog.

earthengine.assets.staging.retentionDays.markdownDescription: Age, in days, after which staged objects are deleted by a Cloud Storage [lifecycle rule](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/lifecycle) scoped to the staging prefix. The rule is installed on first upload and is the safety net for ingestions that outlive the VS Code session. Set to `0` to never install it.

languageModelTools.name: earthengine_runCommand
languageModelTools.userDescription: Run Earth Engine extension commands (open the map, load example layers, open panels, refresh trees).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs a command of the Earth Engine VS Code extension. Use it when the user asks to open the Earth Engine map, show the SEPAL visualization example (map + 4 layers), open the asset manager or the export/import task tables, or refresh a tree. Commands: earthengine.openMap (open the map), earthengine.map.testSepalViz (SEPAL visualization example: map + 4 layers), earthengine.openAssetsPanel, earthengine.openExportTasksPanel, earthengine.openImportTasksPanel, earthengine.refreshAssets, earthengine.refreshTasks, earthengine.refreshDatasets, earthengine.refreshDocs, earthengine.showAuthStatus. For any Earth Engine analysis (filtering, computing, exporting), load the earthengine-python skill and write a Python script instead.

languageModelTools.name: earthengine_addMapLayer
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add any Earth Engine asset (image, image collection, table) to the map.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Adds an Earth Engine asset to the interactive map panel (opens the map if needed). Images are displayed directly, image collections are mosaicked (most recent pixel on top), tables (FeatureCollections) are drawn with ee.FeatureCollection.style(). For images and collections, visParams follows ee.Image.visualize(): bands (1 or 3 band names), min, max (numbers or per-band arrays), palette (array of hex colors), gamma. For tables, visParams follows style(): color, width, fillColor, pointSize, pointShape. Pass {"default": <name or index>} to use a SEPAL visualization preset stored on the asset; an empty visParams uses the first SEPAL preset if any, else EE defaults. Adding a layer with an existing name replaces that layer. Returns the layer index. Only displays an existing asset unchanged: for any filtering by date/region/clouds, compositing, band math, masking, reduction or export, load the earthengine-python skill and write a Python script instead.

visParams.description: Visualization parameters, e.g. {"bands": ["B4", "B3", "B2"], "min": 0, "max": 3000} or {"min": 0, "max": 4000, "palette": ["006633", "E5FFCC", "662A00"]} or, for tables, {"color": "red", "width": 1}.

name.description: Layer name shown in the layer panel. Defaults to the asset id.

opacity.description: Layer opacity between 0 and 1. Defaults to 1.

shown.description: Whether the layer is visible. Defaults to true.

languageModelTools.name: earthengine_setMapView
languageModelTools.userDescription: Center the Earth Engine map on a location.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Centers the interactive Earth Engine map on a latitude/longitude at a given zoom level (opens the map if needed). Zoom ranges from 0 (whole world) to 24; about 3 for a continent, 5-6 for a country, 10-12 for a city, 15+ for streets.

zoom.description: Zoom level. Keeps the current zoom when omitted.

languageModelTools.name: earthengine_listMapLayers
languageModelTools.userDescription: List the layers displayed on the Earth Engine map.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the layers currently on the Earth Engine map with their index, name, visibility, opacity and visualization parameters. Use it before removing a layer or to know what the user is looking at.

languageModelTools.name: earthengine_removeMapLayer
languageModelTools.userDescription: Remove a layer from the Earth Engine map.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Removes one layer from the Earth Engine map, identified by its index (preferred, from earthengine_listMapLayers) or its exact name.

index.description: Layer index as reported by earthengine_listMapLayers.

name.description: Exact layer name, used when index is not given.

languageModelTools.name: earthengine_deleteAsset
languageModelTools.userDescription: Delete an Earth Engine asset (asks for confirmation).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Deletes an asset of the user's Earth Engine project. Folders and image collections are deleted recursively with all their content. Irreversible: the user is asked to confirm. Paths relative to the current project ('my_folder/my_image') are expanded to 'projects/<project>/assets/...'; full 'projects/.../assets/...' paths are used as is.

languageModelTools.name: earthengine_moveAsset
languageModelTools.userDescription: Move or rename an Earth Engine asset (asks for confirmation).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Moves or renames an asset of the user's Earth Engine project. Folders and image collections are moved recursively. The destination is the full new asset path (not the parent folder) and must not already exist nor be inside the source. Paths relative to the current project are expanded to 'projects/<project>/assets/...'.

languageModelTools.name: earthengine_copyAsset
languageModelTools.userDescription: Copy an Earth Engine asset (asks for confirmation).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Copies an asset into the user's Earth Engine project. Folders and image collections are copied recursively. The destination is the full new asset path (not the parent folder) and must not already exist nor be inside the source. Paths relative to the current project are expanded to 'projects/<project>/assets/...'.

languageModelTools.name: earthengine_listTasks
languageModelTools.userDescription: List export/import tasks with state, runtime and EECU cost.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists recent Earth Engine export and import (ingest) tasks of the current project, newest first, or details a single task when 'name' is given. For each task returns: name (full operation name, needed for cancelling), description, kind, state (PENDING, RUNNING, CANCELLING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED), progress, create/start/end times, elapsed (human-readable runtime), runSeconds (exact seconds running, or ran), queuedSeconds (seconds waited before starting), eecuSeconds and eecuHours (batch EECU consumed: the compute cost, billed per EECU-hour; it may be absent or partial while a task is still running), priority, attempt, destinationUris and error message. Only the 100 most recent operations are scanned.

name.description: Full operation name, e.g. 'projects/my-project/operations/ABC123', to get a single task.

states.description: Only return tasks in these states.

limit.description: Maximum number of tasks returned. Defaults to 20.

languageModelTools.name: earthengine_cancelTask
languageModelTools.userDescription: Cancel a pending or running export/import task (asks for confirmation).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Cancels a PENDING or RUNNING Earth Engine export or import task, identified by its full operation name (get it from earthengine_listTasks). Fails if the task already finished.

languageModelTools.name: earthengine_getPythonSetup
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get the active Earth Engine project and the header to start a Python script with.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the active Earth Engine project (null when no profile is active) and the 'header' every Earth Engine Python script should start with: import ee, from vscee import Map, ee.Initialize(project=...). Call it before writing any Earth Engine Python script and use the header verbatim.
